status_summary: A narrower restriction on Chinese companies became operative in defense purchasing during the period. The restriction comes from Section 805 of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2024 (Public Law 118-31, approved 2023-12-22, before the period), not from the FY2026 act (Public Law 119-60), whose own Section 805 concerns technical data. Under it, the Department of War's direct ban on procurement from companies on its Section 1260H list of Chinese military companies, and from entities they control, took effect on 2026-06-30, with an indirect ban on goods incorporating their products from 2027-06-30; the Department published a waiver process. A Federal Register notice of 2026-06-10 published a designation of Chinese military companies, and a trade-press report from July 2026 says the Department issued implementation guidance and that the June 2026 list update added dozens of subsidiaries and affiliates. The restriction covers listed Chinese military companies rather than state-owned enterprises as such, and Department of War purchases rather than all federal procurement; no government-wide rule was found.

timeline.event: The Department of Defense published a notice of availability stating that the Deputy Secretary of Defense determined that the entities listed in the notice satisfy the requirements to be designated Chinese military companies (91 FR 35189, pages 35189 to 35194).
The Section 805 direct ban on Department of War procurement from Section 1260H-listed Chinese military companies and entities they control took effect, with a national-interest waiver process.

title: Bar Chinese state-owned enterprises from bidding on U.S. government procurement
uncertainties: Section 805 was enacted before 2025-01-20 and its 2026 effective date is a statutory schedule; the period's actions are implementation and list updates. The 2026-06-30 date comes from the Department's undated waiver page and is confirmed by the trade-press report, whose date is given as July 2026 from its URL. Public Law 119-60, the FY2026 defense authorization (approved 2025-12-18), was confirmed on GovInfo but its text was not read; a law-firm summary of China provisions names only an AI procurement restriction from it. The same summary reports that the House-passed FY2027 defense bill would refer 1260H entities for government-wide exclusion orders; this was not verified on a primary site and is not an event here. A Federal Register search for state-owned enterprise procurement rules since 2025-01-20 found no FAR or DFARS rule. How many 1260H entries are state-owned was not checked. The 2019 transit rolling stock limit is background only. The section number was checked: the restriction rests on Section 805 of the FY2024 defense authorization law (Public Law 118-31, confirmed on GovInfo, and named as the FY2024 act on the Department's Section 805 page), not on Section 805 of Public Law 119-60 (S. 1071, signed 2025-12-18), which is titled for technical data insufficiencies and is unrelated. The GovInfo table of contents of Public Law 119-60 lists Sec. 845 (modifies procurements from certain Chinese entities) and Sec. 1263 (adds entities to the Chinese military company list), but the section text was beyond the portion of the page that could be read, so their effect on Section 805 is not verified. The text of Section 805 of Public Law 118-31 was not read, because the GovInfo HTML of that law was cut off before Title VIII; its dates and scope come from the Department's page. A Federal Register search for Chinese military companies since 2025-01-20 returned no FAR or DFARS implementing rule. The designation notice's entity list was not visible in the fetched text, and the 2026-06-10 notice does not mention Section 805.
